svg.title: East Corridor plan — Masterplan 05 Combined Zones
svg.desc: Study plan of the 1,277-block multimodal East Corridor carrying a four-lane divided highway, a double-track passenger railway, a protected pedestrian route and a utility reserve from a terminal roundabout east of MainStreet America to the Combined Zones Gateway, with a single Data District interchange.
svg.text: C1 · EAST CORRIDOR — HIGHWAY AND RAILWAY
ONE 56-BLOCK RESERVATION · MAINSTREET EAST TO THE GATEWAY · 1,277 BLOCKS · NORTH UP
ZERO CATALOGED SURFACE INTERSECTIONS · ALL Y VALUES REQUIRE SURVEY

g.text: DATA DISTRICT — cataloged, south edge z=-172
C01 EAST (subsurface, ISSUE-002) — 18 blocks plan, ~17 below grade
ramps develop south — north flank kept clear for rail

svg.text: NORTH FLANK RAIL — platforms face the pedestrian route;
district reached at grade, no station structures.
+12 blocks slope easement each side = 80 total land take.
Highway mainline centerline — 4-lane divided, 85 km/h declared design speed
Double-track passenger railway on the north flank — the world's first rail
Local road tying into a cataloged existing road (L1 Ravensreach, L3 Observatory)
Provisional only — L2 has no cataloged gate; Grand Avenue skew needs a fix
Data District interchange: one interchange, four ramps south, one bridge
Subsurface cataloged feature — C01 East is contested under ISSUE-002
Geometry uses orthogonal legs and exact 45° diagonals only. Three curve vertices against a budget of four, each chamfered
spiral–arc–spiral (1:16→1:12→1:8→1:6→1:8→1:12→1:16). Northward vertices use R=140 to hold a 120-block rail radius.
One interchange, not two: minimum off-off / on-on gore spacing is 305 blocks and the district tangent is 265, so a second
interchange is geometrically impossible rather than merely tight. Ramps develop south because westbound right-side ramps
would otherwise run into the railway and pedestrian route on the north flank.
Clearance verified against all 1,215 catalog records: zero surface intersections; nearest surface feature 50 blocks.
A database non-overlap check is not a terrain, hydrology, entity, ownership, or chunk-generation clearance.
